Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Sri Imran Khan, learned AGA, for the State, apprised the Court that he has received the instructions, therefore, the instant anticipatory bail application may be finally disposed off.

2. Heard Sri Shitlesh Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Janardan Yadav, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Imran Khan, learned AGA, for the State.
3.

The instant anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on anticipatory bail in FIR/Case Crime No.204 of 2022, under Sections 420,406,
467,468, 471, 34 and 120-B IPC, Police Station Bilariyaganj, District Azamgarh during pendency of the trial.

4. sentences.text: 1 having share broker Firm and if he will invest money in their Firm then he will earn huge amount of profit and due to their inducement informant invested Rs.Seventy Lacs in the Firm, known as Zehan Enterprises.

It is further mentioned in the FIR that a very decent amount has also been transferred by informant in the account of co-accused Syed. Mohd. Bilal and according to the FIR, the Firm was registered in the name of co-accused Syed Mohd. Bilal.

It is further mentioned in the FIR that accused persons also provided the informant some undated cheques but when informant checked the balance then he found that there was no money in the Bank Account which was mentioned on the cheques and subsequently informant came to know that the Firm of the accused persons was not legal one.
5.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that on the basis of false allegation applicant has been made accused in the present matter.
6. He further submits that actually applicant is the brother of principal accused-Bilal and only due to this reason he has been made accused in the present matter.

7. He further submits that even from the FIR it reflects that the alleged Firm was of co-accused Syed.
Mohd. Bilal and in his account money was transferred.
8. He further submits that applicant is not having any concern with the alleged fraud and he did not receive any money from any one.

9. He further submits that even from the FIR it reflects that no offence is made out as if anyone made some investment for getting profit and he failed to receive the profit then no criminal liability could be fastened.

10. He further submits that applicant is not having any previous criminal history and investigation of the case is still pending since 2022 and now police is trying to arrest the applicant, therefore,
considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, applicant should be released on anticipatory bail.

11. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant however opposed the prayerfor anticipatory bail and submitted that however in the FIR it is mentioned that only Rs.Seventy Lacs were taken by applicant and other accused persons from the informant but in fact crores of Rupees have been misappropriated by applicant and other accused persons under the pretext to give profit to the informant and subsequently it was found that their Firm was fake Firm.
12. However, both the learned counsels could not dispute the fact that as per allegation the Firm was of Syed. Mohd. Bilal and the money was also transferred in the Bank account of co-accused Syed.
Mohd. Bilal and applicant is his brother.

13. However, learned counsel for the informant further argued that during investigation one Afzal categorically stated before the Investigating Officer that Rs.Four Lacs Fifty Thousand has been given by him to the applicant but he fairly conceded that according to Afzal, he gave such huge amount in Syed Mohammad Talib vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64823276/
2 cash and except his statement there is no other evidence in this regard on record.

sentences.text: 14. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
15. However, from the FIR it reflects that huge amount of money of informant has been misappropriated but it reflects that principal accused in the present matter is co-accused Syed.

Mohd. Bilal, brother of the applicant and he is the person, who was the Proprietor of the Firm,namely, Zehan Enterprises and in his account money was transferred and there is no allegation in the FIR against the applicant that he also received any money from any one.

16. However, it appears that during investigation one person stated to Investigating Officer that he also gave Rs.Four Lacs Fifty Thousand to the applicant but even from his statement it reflects that Rs.Four Lacs Fifty Thousand was given by him to the applicant as cash.
17. Applicant is the brother of principal accused Syed.

Mohd. Bilal, therefore, argument advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant that only being brother of co-accused, applicant has been made accused in the present matter, cannot be completely dis-believed, considering the fact that number of other accused persons were also the family members of the principal accused Syed. Mohd. Bilarl.

18. Further, applicant is not having any previous criminal history and FIR of the present case was lodged in the year 2022 but investigation of the case is still pending and it appears, now police is trying to arrest the applicant.

19. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail till the conclusion of the trial.
20. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail anticipatory application is allowed.
